title: Parameters That Fit in Memory
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: DGX Evaluation for Textbook Generation
description: A memory slider moves three limits along a parameter-count axis, showing the most parameters that fit at 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit precision, with five candidate language models plotted as points.

learningObjectives: Calculate the memory a model's weights need from its parameter count and precision
Determine the largest model that fits in a given amount of memory at each precision
Explain why a real model needs more memory than the formula predicts
prerequisites: A bit, a byte, and a gigabyte
That a language model is a large set of numeric parameters

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with immediate feedback, followed by a worked calculation
keyQuestions: At what memory size does each model first fit at 4-bit?
How does halving the precision change the number of parameters that fit?
Why is a 4-bit download larger than four bits per parameter?
What uses the memory that the formula sets aside?
commonMisconceptions: A model fits if its download is smaller than memory. The context and the operating system need memory too.
A 4-bit model uses exactly four bits per parameter. Real quantized files keep some layers at higher precision.
A GPU with unified memory has its own memory budget. It shares one pool with the CPU.
assessmentOpportunities: Work out the limits for a memory size by hand, then check with the slider
State the precision a given model needs on a given system and explain what could make the estimate too optimistic
